details.completeness_justification: The candidate summary adequately covers the core material meaning of K1, K2, K3, K4, K5, K6, K8, and K9. K1 is covered in S2, S3, and S4 with revenue, EBITDA, and portfolio growth. K2 is fully covered in S7, S8, and S9 with all revenue segments and changes. K3 is covered in S8 and S10 with installment loans in Europe and issuance amount. K4 is covered in S10 with smartphone financing in Kenya and Uganda and portfolio size. K5 is covered in S11 with Tanzania entry and motorcycle financing focus. K6 is covered in S20 with AI voice agents at call centers. K8 is covered in S13 with the EUR 275 million bond issuance as the largest in history. K9 is covered in S15 with dividend distribution and yield. However, K7 (EUR 40 million bond tap in March 2025) is missing entirely. K10 (impairment expense increase) is missing. K11 (regulatory challenge in Moldova) is missing. K12 (post-reporting period funding from P2P and Kenya borrowings) is missing. The omissions of K7, K10, K11, and K12—particularly the high-importance K7, K10, and K11—prevent the summary from achieving a 'Yes' rating, but the strong coverage of the other high-importance criteria supports a 'Generally yes' assessment.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary demonstrates strong internal logical coherence. All statements build upon each other without contradiction: performance drivers (S1) align with reported metrics (S2-S5), revenue composition shifts are clearly explained (S6-S9), geographic expansion is logically presented (S10-S11), capital actions support balance sheet comments (S12-S14), and risk management outcomes align with stated strategies (S17). The summary flows from performance highlights to segment breakdowns, then to capital actions and risk metrics, forming a coherent narrative. No material contradictions, logical gaps, or organizational issues are present. Repetition is minimal and serves emphasis rather than confusion.
